findings.title: fire_unit_until still waits for the whole firing
findings.description: `scripts/cutover_common.py:343-365` starts the pass with `run(["mt-run", *mt_run_args], ..., stream=True)` before calling `wait_for_unit_or_line(...)`. `run()` in `scripts/cutover_common.py` delegates to `subprocess.run`; `stream=True` only disables output capture and still waits for the child process to exit. `deploy/mt-run#start_and_stream` starts the unit with `systemctl start --no-block`, then loops `while is_running(unit); do sleep 2; done` until the unit is inactive. Therefore `fire_unit_until()` cannot observe the trailing-phase marker while the unit is still active, and `if reached and unit_active(unit)` at `scripts/cutover_common.py:360-362` cannot stop it early. This defeats the #22 fix: the cutover still waits for the unbounded firing/backfill to finish. The new `test/unit/test_cutover_921.py#TestBoundedFiringAndRecord` patches `cutover_common.run` to return immediately, so it validates a non-blocking seam that the real `mt-run` wrapper does not provide. Fire the unit from Python with `systemctl start --no-block` and poll the journal directly, or add a bounded wrapper mode that returns immediately.

findings.title: Sudoers aliases grant much broader root execution than the comment claims
findings.description: `deploy/sudoers.d/manta-ops:7-13` says “Exactly the commands those scripts issue, nothing wider”, but `MT_RUN = /usr/local/bin/mt-run *` allows any argument vector to `mt-run`. In `deploy/mt-run#run_production_mt`, any unrecognized verb is forwarded to `/opt/manta-trading/.venv/bin/mt "$@"` as root after sourcing `/etc/manta-trading.env`; that includes arbitrary `mt data ...` maintenance commands, not just `minute`, `daily`, and `kalshi`. `MT_UNITS` also allows `stop/start/restart` for every `mt-*` unit, not the named units the scripts use. Restrict the aliases to exact command/argument combinations used by the cutover, or put a validating wrapper in `/usr/local/sbin` that only accepts an allowlist.

findings.title: Human-readable verify labels are used as control flow
findings.description: `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:200-211` loops while `"[WAIT]" in text`, and `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:261-278` decides acceptance with `"FAIL" not in verify_text and "[WAIT]" not in verify_text`. `_repair()` returns raw stdout+stderr from `scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py#run_verify`, which prints user-facing `[PASS]`, `[FAIL]`, and `[WAIT]` labels. The repair CLI already has `EXIT_OK`/`EXIT_REFUSED`, but `_repair()` only logs the return code instead of using it as the contract. This violates the project convention “NEVER use user-accessible labels as logical structure” and creates a loose untyped boundary where any log text containing `FAIL` or `WAIT` changes cutover behavior. Return a structured result (JSON or a typed Python function result) and use exit status/fields for control flow.

findings.title: Cagg freshness probe can crash on a never-successful policy
findings.description: `src/manta_trading/data/gaps/repair_921.py:202-209` selects `stats.last_successful_finish` directly. The existing project code at `src/manta_trading/market/maintenance/cagg_freshness.py:68-80` documents that TimescaleDB stores `-infinity` for a refresh policy created but never completed, that psycopg raises `DataError` while fetching it, and therefore normalizes it with `nullif(..., '-infinity'::timestamptz)`. This new probe omits that normalization and has no handler in `run_verify`, so a fresh/failed policy makes `--verify` crash instead of reporting a controlled WAIT. The raw-table `max(created_at)` query at `src/manta_trading/data/gaps/repair_921.py:212-220` also has no `SET LOCAL statement_timeout`, despite scanning `minute_ohlcv` by session time; SQL rules require bounded long-running queries. Use the established `nullif` pattern, set a statement timeout, and add a regression test with `-infinity` job stats.

findings.title: New per-cycle truncated-day scan has no load-tier resource bound
findings.description: `src/manta_trading/data/acquisition/daemon/minute.py:298-303` now calls `_build_truncated_index()` before every trailing phase. `_build_truncated_index()` at `src/manta_trading/data/acquisition/daemon/minute.py:349-373` delegates to `src/manta_trading/data/gaps/repair_921.py#build_truncated_day_index`, whose SQL scans raw `minute_ohlcv` with a 600s timeout. The new unit tests cover wiring and timeout logging, but `test/load/test_921_minute_session_mass_nfr.py:1-68` covers only `fetch_session_mass`; no load-tier test asserts latency, throughput, or resource bounds for this new daemon DB scan. The Python/SQL review rules require a load test for database/environment-layer hot paths and CI gating for slices touching them. Add a realistic prod-shaped load test for the truncated-day scan and assert a latency/resource budget.
